what: Mid-America Apartment Communities owns about 100,000 apartments, almost all of them in the American Sun Belt, and rents them to households on one-year leases.
customers: Renters in Atlanta, Dallas, Austin, Tampa, Charlotte, Nashville and other southern cities.
money: rent from the stabilised apartment portfolio
newly built or acquired communities and fee income
moat: Scale concentrated in a small number of fast-growing metros, which makes leasing, maintenance and pricing cheaper per apartment than scattered ownership.
risks: A great deal of new apartment supply has been delivered in exactly the Sun Belt markets it owns
Rent growth has slowed to near zero as a result, with revenue flat at $2.2B
opportunities: $623M of free cash flow and analysts see about 18% upside, with 25 covering the stock
New apartment construction starts have collapsed, so the supply wave should clear by 2027
People keep moving to the Sun Belt, and buying a house there is still far dearer than renting
watch: New supply deliveries in its markets and same-store rent growth.
